source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A Muslim client has an order for a cough syrup that is an alcohol-based elixir. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Alcohol is prohibited in Islam; the nurse verifies the order and requests an alcohol-free alternative.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Cultural diversity exercises (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Dimetapp DM is an elixir. It is an alcohol — based medication. Alcohol is pmhibited among Muslim patient.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A Jehovah's Witness client with massive GI bleeding has several orders. Which should the nurse verify with the physician?
questions.rationale: Jehovah's Witnesses refuse blood and blood products; non-blood volume expanders are acceptable.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Cultural diversity exercises (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Among Jehovah's Witness, administration of blood and blood products is forbidden.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which food should not be served to a Seventh-day Adventist client?
questions.rationale: Seventh-day Adventists avoid scavenger seafood such as shrimp, crab and squid, and fish without scales.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Cultural diversity exercises (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Seventh Day Adventist religion prohibits scavenger fishes like shrimp. crab, squid, fishes with no scales like catfish and eel.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A Jewish client following a kosher diet receives roast beef with a glass of milk. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Kosher rules prohibit combining meat and milk and forbid pork and scavenger fish.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Cultural diversity exercises (PDF p. 22)
questions.quote: Meat and milk combination, rxyrk, and scavenger fishes are prohibited.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse discloses a client's HIV status to the client's neighbor, who is not involved in his care. This is:
questions.rationale: Disclosing confidential information to an inappropriate third party is invasion of privacy, even if true.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Torts (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: Is disclosing confidential information to an inappropriate third party (subjects the nurse to invasion of privacy even if the information is true).

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse tells a confused client, "If you leave your room again, I will tie you to the bed." The nurse may be liable for:
questions.rationale: Assault is the threat of touching without consent; battery is the actual touching.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Critical thinking: leadership (PDF p. 38)
questions.quote: Assault is threatening a client; threat of touching another person without his/her consent.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The nurse gives an injection after the client clearly refused it. The nurse may be liable for:
questions.rationale: Battery is the actual carrying out of touching without consent, including treatment without consent.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Torts (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: Battery. Is the actual carrying out ofa threat.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A hospital refuses to let a recovered patient go home until he pays his bill. This may be:
questions.rationale: Detaining a client without legal justification is false imprisonment.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Torts (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: occurs when a client is not allowed to Igaye a health care facility when there is no legal justification to detain the client.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse posts false statements online claiming a doctor is incompetent. This is:
questions.rationale: Defamation in print, writing or pictures is libel; spoken defamation is slander.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Torts (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: Libel. Is defamation by means of print. writing. or pictures.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: To prove nursing malpractice, which element must be shown along with duty, breach and injury?
questions.rationale: Malpractice requires duty, breach of duty, injury and a causal link between the breach and the injury.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Malpractice (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: A causal relationship between the breach of duty and the client subsequent injury.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which nursing action meets the standard of care?
options: Holding digoxin for an apical pulse of 56
Running KCl IV with urine output of 15 mL/hr
Skipping ordered hourly I&O in renal failure
Delaying a report of suspected abuse
questions.rationale: Holding digoxin for a pulse below 60 follows the standard of care; the others fall below it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Critical thinking: leadership (PDF p. 38)
questions.quote: Digoxin may cause bradycardia. It is not administered if the apical rate is 60 bpm or slower..

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client found on the floor is helped back to bed. Which entry belongs on the incident report?
options: "Client was found lying on the floor."
"Client became restless and tried to get up."
questions.rationale: Incident reports state only observed facts, without opinions or assumptions.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Critical thinking: ethical and legal (PDF p. 30)
questions.quote: Documentation should be factual and objective. Avoid opinions, inte relations, and legally-im licatin ' statements.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Where should a completed incident report be kept?
questions.rationale: The incident report is a quality tool; it is not copied or placed in the client's record and does not replace chart documentation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Incident reports (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: Thc report form should not bc copied or placed in the client's record.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A nurse made an error in a narrative note. The correct way to fix it is to:
questions.rationale: Never erase or use correction fluid; draw a single line, initial and date the error.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Documentation (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: In case of error. draw one line through the error. initial and date.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When taking a telephone order from a physician, the nurse should first:
options: Read the order back to confirm it
Wait for a written order before acting
Ask a nursing attendant to listen
questions.rationale: Repeat (read back) the order, record it with date, time and "T.O.", and have it countersigned per policy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Telephone orders (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Repeat ("read back") the order to the physician and record the order.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A medication dose ordered is higher than recommended, and the physician cannot be reached. The nurse should:
options: Skip the dose and tell no one
questions.rationale: Question an inappropriate order; if the physician can't be reached, go through the supervisor.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Critical thinking: ethical and legal (PDF p. 29)
questions.quote: When the nurse is unable to contact the physician, he/she should seek the help of the nursing supervisor.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An unidentified, unconscious accident victim needs an emergency craniotomy. Regarding consent, the nurse should:
options: Proceed to surgery; consent is waived
questions.rationale: In life-saving emergencies written consent may be waived; the emergency is documented.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Critical thinking: ethical and legal (PDF p. 30)
questions.quote: In case of emergency, to save the life of a client, written consent may be waived.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A nurse finds a coworker about to inject herself with a drug in the medication room. The most appropriate initial action is to:
questions.rationale: Report through proper channels; client safety comes first and administration handles impaired staff.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Critical thinking: ethical and legal (PDF p. 30)
questions.quote: The nurse should report the situation to the nursing supervisor.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The nurse respects a client's decision to choose her own treatment for breast cancer after the doctor explained options. This is the principle of:
questions.rationale: Autonomy is the right to accept or refuse treatment; paternalism is deciding for others.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Critical thinking: leadership (PDF p. 38)
questions.quote: Autonomy implies the client's right to accept or refuse any treatment.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Hiding medicine the client refused in his fruit juice violates the principle of:
questions.rationale: The client has the right to refuse treatment; covert administration violates autonomy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Critical thinking: ethical and legal (PDF p. 31)
questions.quote: Autonomy is the right to accept or refuse any treatment. It is the right for self-determination.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When applying a physical restraint, the nurse ties it to the:
questions.rationale: Secure restraints to the bed frame, not side rails, using a quick-release tie; check frequently and release periodically.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Use of restraints (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Secure restraints at thc bed frame, not on the side rails.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which order for restraints is legally unacceptable?
options: An order with the reason stated
questions.rationale: PRN orders for restraints are not acceptable; each episode needs a specific order and consent.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Use of restraints (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: PRN order for restraints application is legally unacceptable.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which client should the nurse see first?
options: Client with a rash after a new drug
questions.rationale: Sudden silence in an asthmatic suggests severe airway obstruction; airway comes first.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Prioritization exercises (PDF p. 34)
questions.quote: When the wheezing in a patient with asthma suddenly disappears- this implies complete airway obstruction.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which pair of clients may share a room?
questions.rationale: Neither condition is infectious; different airborne infections or an infection beside pin sites risk cross-contamination.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Rooming-in exercises (PDF p. 36)
questions.quote: There is no danger of cross contamination. Acute pancreatitis is inflammatory condition, not an infection.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which diseases require an airborne-precaution private room (or cohorting)?
questions.rationale: Airborne infections ("MTV"): measles, TB, varicella/disseminated zoster need private rooms.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Rooming-in (PDF p. 35)
questions.quote: Clients with airborne infections should be confined in private rooms; cohorting is allowed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which task can the nurse delegate to a nursing attendant?
questions.rationale: Routine, stable tasks may be delegated; assessment, teaching, evaluation and complex care stay with the RN.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Critical thinking: leadership (PDF p. 37)
questions.quote: The nursing assistant/health aide can perform enema.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A head nurse makes all decisions alone and gives commands during a mass casualty incident. Her leadership style is:
questions.rationale: Autocratic leadership keeps strong control and is effective in emergencies.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Leadership styles (PDF p. 31)
questions.quote: It is effective in emergency situations, as the leader needs to take control of the situation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Staff follow a senior nurse because they admire and identify with her. This is which type of power?
questions.rationale: Referent power is based on attraction and admiration; legitimate power comes from position.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Types of power (PDF p. 32)
questions.quote: Referent Based on attracuon.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In Lewin's change theory, staff identifying the problem and gathering evidence for change is the stage of:
questions.rationale: Unfreezing: recognize the need; moving: implement; refreezing: stabilize the change.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Change process (PDF p. 32)
questions.quote: Unfreezing. The problem is identified and individuals Involved gather fxts and evidence supporting a basis for change.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A quality team reviews charts of discharged patients for compliance with care standards. This is a:
questions.rationale: Retrospective audits examine records after discharge; concurrent audits occur during the stay.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Performance improvement (PDF p. 33)
questions.quote: evaluation method used to inspect medical record after the patient's discharge for documentation of compliance with the standards.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Two nurses resolve a scheduling dispute by working together until both are fully satisfied. This is:
questions.rationale: Collaboration is true problem-solving, a win-win strategy; compromise means each gives up something.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Conflict management (PDF p. 33)
questions.quote: Collaboration True problem — solving
